text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000083 bills 99215 well above risk-adjusted expectation in every complexity tier, including on many low-complexity patients, but too few charts came back to confirm or rule out upcoding.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The claims pattern is consistent with upcoding rather than a sicker panel. The 99215 share runs well above the all-provider rate in every condition-count band, not just among complex patients, and nearly half of the 99215s fall on patients with 0 or 1 chronic conditions. The sampled low-complexity 99215s include visits coded only for a follow-up (Z09: C0040814, C0040840), an upper respiratory infection (J06.9: C0041377, C0041708) or abdominal pain (R10.9: C0039958, C0040143), which would rarely need high-complexity decision-making. Even so, documentation cannot settle the question: both documented 99215s fell below the billed level (C0040968, and C0042039, an obesity-only patient documented at moderate MDM with 23 minutes), but two charts are far too few to judge. The single note claiming moderate-or-higher data reviewed with no lab or test line on the claim is weak evidence at most. A reviewer should first request records for the low-complexity 99215 claims listed here, starting with the Z09, J06.9 and R10.9 visits, and check whether the documented MDM and time support level 5 or look templated."}
